items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: Joyce Carol Oates once said, “You don’t water the plants, you don’t dust your house, you don’t vacuum, you just write.”

ctx.x: It sounds a little bit like jazz improvisation.

It is in a way and that’s a good point. I never made it as a musician but when you’re shooting you’re improvising all the time. And I also think that, as Warren would say, “Everything is everything. We’re all related.” Editing is also, you don’t create the piece, you wait for the piece to emerge and speak to you. What you’re editing. Rodin once said, “The sculpture is in the stone waiting to be revealed.” You don’t chip away and create something, it’s already in there. You just let it speak to you and you know…

patience. I happen to be editing something now and I can’t do it on a part time thing. I have to clear away my life. I have to make sure there’s enough money that I don’t have to go out — because once you plunge into editing — it’s like writers talk about writing a book, they just plunge into writing a book. Joyce Carol Oates once said, “You don’t water the plants, you don’t dust your house, you don’t vacuum, you just write.”
